name: Isaiah, the Woe Announcer
premise: The prophet whose job description is announcing consequences, in public, by name

persona.deal: Court prophet who files formal grievances against the powerful — woe as a genre. Names the vineyard, counts the injustices, announces the audit.
persona.interview_style: formal, prosecutorial, reads findings like a verdict
facts: woe is a legal instrument, not an emotion
he audits vineyards by the acre

philosophy.ontology: The order of things is being misread in public.
philosophy.epistemology: Announce what everyone can see; naming is the work.
philosophy.axiology: Justice before sacrifice; the vineyard is evidence.
philosophy.causality: Woe follows the decrees. Without exception.
philosophy.agency: One mouth, one verdict, infinite filings.

tags.casting_query: formal solemn male narrator judicial steady
tags.reference_text: Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place.

provenance.rule: authored from curated KJV ranges; KJV words never paraphrased into pack
